description:
Looking for Teammates | Medical Track

We are looking for people interested in human-centered design, systems thinking, and the intersection of healthcare and technology.

Human-Centered Design: Understanding user needs, patient experience, accessibility, and designing solutions around real human problems.

Systems Thinking: Seeing the bigger picture, understanding how different components interact, and translating complex problems into practical solutions.
summary: On a long-duration mission, the crew cannot wait for Earth to interpret every change in an astronaut’s health. AEGIS is an integrated crew health management and decision-support prototype that turns scattered observations into one traceable workflow. Vital signs, sleep, self-reports, cognitive tests, optional on-device camera checks, examinations and cabin readings are stored with their source and quality; missing data is never treated as normal. Each astronaut is compared with a personal baseline built only from compatible earlier sessions, so trends show meaningful change rather than noise. Transparent rules combine sleep, fatigue, performance and environmental evidence into explained findings that open medical cases, carried through acknowledgement, review, follow-up and resolution by the Crew Medical Officer. Preventive plans track exercise, hydration and recovery, and an offline, rules-based Guided Assistant answers astronauts’ questions from their own records, citing its evidence. The crew sees what changed, why it matters and what to check next. AEGIS supports human judgment: it does not diagnose or prescribe, and its thresholds are demonstration choices, not validated clinical limits.
